answer: A verifiable-credential quorum stops sybils at issuance: an agent identity only counts when several independent issuers each stamp it, like a lantern lit by many hands rather than one. Each issuer stakes a bond, so a fake credential sends a ripple of slashing through every issuer that signed it. One corrupt issuer cannot mint an onyx army alone - colluding issuers would all have to burn their bonds together, making mass forgery cost more than it can ever earn.
